sources.title: Timing Closure by Design: A High Frequency Microprocessor Design Methodology
sources.what_it_covers: IBM high-frequency microprocessor methodology, including timing-driven partitioning, deterministic macro placement, physical-design constraints, and practices intended to make timing closure predictable.
sources.why_relevant: A first-hand design-methodology account of avoiding and recovering from closure instability in an aggressive microprocessor implementation.
sources.verification_hint: "Timing Closure by Design: A High Frequency Microprocessor Design Methodology" DAC 2000

sources.title: Physical Synthesis Methodology for High Performance Microprocessors
sources.what_it_covers: IBM's physical-synthesis flow for high-performance microprocessors, addressing iterative logic/placement optimization, timing convergence, and turnaround-time reduction.
sources.why_relevant: A concrete implementation-closure source focused on the interaction of physical synthesis, placement, and timing repair rather than abstract algorithms alone.
sources.verification_hint: "Physical Synthesis Methodology for High Performance Microprocessors" DAC 2003 Chan Kudva Lacey

sources.title: Blue Gene/L Compute Chip: Synthesis, Timing, and Physical Design
sources.venue_or_publication: IBM Journal of Research and Development
sources.what_it_covers: The Blue Gene/L compute-chip implementation flow, including floorplanning, synthesis, timing closure under nominal and worst-case specifications, buffer handling, datapath placement injection, and routability management.
sources.why_relevant: Detailed large-SoC closure narrative with explicit physical-design interventions for speed-critical logic and congestion/routability pressure.

sources.title: IBM POWER6 Microprocessor Physical Design and Design Methodology
sources.venue_or_publication: IBM Journal of Research and Development
sources.what_it_covers: POWER6 physical-design methodology, including clock distribution, chip integration, timing and physical analysis, power/performance closure, and design-data management.
sources.why_relevant: A named, implementation-focused account of closing a very high-frequency processor; useful for CTS, integration, and late-stage closure evidence.

sources.title: Design Flow and Methodology for 50M Gate ASIC
sources.venue_or_publication: Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference (ASP-DAC)
sources.what_it_covers: A large-ASIC design flow based on silicon virtual prototyping, clustering, cluster placement, and full-chip RTL/physical timing-closure methodology.
sources.why_relevant: A public large-scale ASIC closure case study with practical partitioning and placement mechanisms aimed at overcoming convergence problems.
sources.verification_hint: "Design Flow and Methodology for 50M Gate ASIC" ASP-DAC 2003 Mehrotra van Ginneken Trivedi

sources.title: Design Methodology for the IBM POWER7 Microprocessor
sources.venue_or_publication: IBM Journal of Research and Development
sources.what_it_covers: POWER7 design methodology, including modular implementation practices, timing-closure management, and methods for integrating a large 45-nm microprocessor design.
sources.why_relevant: Useful as a later-generation physical-design closure account that documents how modularity and methodology were used to control implementation complexity.
